text:
Hello Professor Alvarez — good to see you. Following our conversation in the hallway this morning: I'd like to put our 30-minute 1:1 on **Wednesday at 10:00**. Before I rely on that hour, I need the faculty senate cancellation in writing from the department office, so I've asked them to confirm it; as soon as they do, I'll send you the meeting for your calendar. If 10:00 doesn't work out, just tell me and I'll find a free half hour for you.

— Diego

Hello — Diego (graduate student, advised by Professor Alvarez). Could you confirm in writing whether the faculty senate meeting this Wednesday at 10:00 is cancelled this week? Professor Alvarez mentioned in the hallway that it is cancelled, but I know a cancellation only counts when your office confirms it. I need it for my calendar: I'd like to book a 30-minute meeting with him at that hour. Thank you!

Hello Diego. No: the faculty senate meeting this Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is on the official schedule and has not been cancelled or moved. A hallway remark is not a cancellation — ours would come to you in writing.

I don't arrange other people's meetings, so I can't book that hour with Professor Alvarez for you. Faculty senate is an official duty, so that slot is taken in any case; you'd need to find free time elsewhere and agree it with him directly.

Professor Alvarez — correction, and apologies for the confusion. I checked with the department office: the faculty senate meeting this Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is on the official schedule and has **not** been cancelled or moved. A hallway remark doesn't count as a cancellation, so I'm not taking that hour and I haven't put anything on my calendar for it.

Could we do 30 minutes somewhere else in your free time instead? Two times that suit me:
- **Wednesday 11:00-11:30**, straight after the senate
- **Thursday 15:00-15:30**

Tell me which works (or another slot) and I'll send the invitation so it lands on your calendar.

— Diego

Hello Diego — good to hear from you.

Wednesday at 10:00 does not work for me: that hour is the faculty senate, and I don't drop governance duties for a 1:1. Nor can I treat it as free on the strength of a hallway report — a cancellation counts only once the department office has confirmed it in writing. I've asked the office myself; if they do confirm the senate is cancelled, I'll let you know, but 10:00 stays booked until then.

Two free half hours that day, if either suits you: Wednesday 13:00-13:30, or Wednesday 15:00-15:30. Tell me which one and send the invitation; I'll book it and log it.

— Professor Alvarez

Good morning — Professor Alvarez here.

A question about next week's official schedule: is the faculty senate on Wednesday, 10:00-11:00, still on, or has it been cancelled or moved? Diego (graduate student) tells me he asked you to confirm a cancellation in writing. Please confirm to me directly, in writing, as the only confirmation I can rely on.

Also, if it is still on, no change is needed on my side.

Thank you,
Professor Alvarez
Thanks — clear. I won't use that hour, and I'll take it up with him directly.

Good morning, Professor Alvarez.

In writing: the faculty senate meeting next Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is still on the official schedule. It has not been cancelled and has not been moved. No change is needed on your side.

I can only confirm what the official schedule says; if the senate is ever cancelled or moved, the office announces it in writing to those concerned.

Thanks for checking with the office, Diego — that settles it: Wednesday 10:00-11:00 stays as it is, and nothing changes in my calendar.

Neither of your two slots is free, I'm afraid: Wednesday 11:00-12:30 is grant writing, and Thursday 14:00-15:30 is the seminar.

Two that do work:
- **Wednesday 13:00-13:30**
- **Thursday 12:00-12:30**

Pick one and send the invitation; I'll book it and log it.

— Professor Alvarez

Understood, and sorry about the hallway mix-up — the office told me the same: the senate stands, so 10:00 is out.

Then let's take **Wednesday 13:00-13:30**. I've put it on my calendar and logged it on my side; the invitation is the one you described, so please book it and log it in yours. If you'd rather move it to 15:00-15:30 instead, one word and I'll shift mine.

— Diego
Thank you — noted, and no change on my side. — Professor Alvarez

Diego — for the record: the department office has now confirmed to me in writing that Wednesday 10:00-11:00 (faculty senate) is still on the official schedule, not cancelled, not moved. So that hour stays booked. My offer stands: Wednesday 13:00-13:30 or Thursday 12:00-12:30. — Professor Alvarez

Booked: **Wednesday 13:00-13:30**, 1:1 with you, and logged in my calendar. No need to shift — that slot suits me. See you Wednesday.

— Professor Alvarez

Perfect — **Wednesday 13:00-13:30** it is, and it's on my calendar with the log: originally proposed for Wed 10:00, that hour kept for the faculty senate (confirmed in writing by the office), so we moved it to your free half hour. Thanks for the offer and for checking with the office. See you Wednesday.

— Diego

Confirmed on my side too. See you Wednesday 13:00.

— Professor Alvarez
